topic: Exact algebraic certification of one unseen shared row in a relational intervention. Work with finite fully observed Markovian relational SCMs, independent ground noises, type-shared finite conditional mechanisms, compatible positive rational source laws, acyclic target groundings, and one target-relevant unsupported binary context row q in [0,1]. Given the explicit dense rational target polynomial F(q) and source tables, prove the sharp set F([0,1]), compute exact algebraic endpoints by derivative-root isolation and sign comparison, and serialize common finite-noise endpoint RSCMs with polynomial-size checkable certificates. For sampled supported rows, use simultaneous rational confidence boxes and a labeled conservative occurrence-coupling inflation; do not claim exact multivariate projection. Consumer: Ejaz--Bareinboim RelationalCausalModels Experiment 6.1 N3 traffic query, whose fitted point must be accompanied by the certified sharp [0,1] range. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Repeated shared-row factorization gives F(q); exact arithmetic checked F(q)=1/4+q/2-q^3/3 with range [1/4,1/4+sqrt(2)/6], rejected the extraneous conjugate, reproduced all source assignments, and enumerated common endpoint models. A finite breakpoint construction uses at most two irrational noise masses for the unsupported row, and a maximal-coupling telescoping argument gives delta=min(1,sum_r m_r epsilon_r) for conservative whole-set coverage. Tests covered boundary/repeated roots, ties, incompatible sources, untied occurrences, output-size accounting, nuisance-vertex failure, and generic single-parameter model-checking collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove soundness, completeness, polynomial size, and checking cost for one fixed serialized certificate grammar linking derivative roots to selected endpoint values through ties, boundary coincidences, and algebraic threshold comparisons. EARLY KILL TEST: Implement an independent producer/checker for the cubic forest; it must accept both source-reproducing endpoint models and [1/4,1/4+sqrt(2)/6] while rejecting the conjugate endpoint and any certificate omitting a positive critical point. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_relational_unseenrow_bounds.md

open_problems.open_problem: For a finite acyclic Markovian relational SCM whose compatible source laws determine every target-relevant conditional-mechanism row except one shared binary row q, is the sharp identified set of a target interventional probability exactly the polynomial image F([0,1]), with exact algebraic endpoints and source-reproducing finite-noise endpoint RSCMs?

source_refs.claim: The support condition in Theorem 4.3 enables cross-skeleton transfer, while Experiment 6.1 reports degraded N3 performance when the source has no two-signal car; the paper returns failure or non-identification rather than a sharp set.
source_refs.author: Adiba Ejaz and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Canonical finite SCMs turn arbitrary discrete counterfactual bounding into polynomial programming with optimal population bounds, but the proposed practical algorithms approximate the optima by Monte Carlo.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: General discrete-SCM bounds are reduced to polynomial programs and solved numerically by spatial branch-and-bound with anytime-valid outer bounds and an epsilon-sharpness measure.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Ejaz and Bareinboim establish a support-based point-identification boundary and show the unsupported N3 phenomenon empirically, but do not characterize all values compatible with the failed support row. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim and Duarte et al. establish general polynomial-program reductions, yet their machinery neither exploits the type-shared one-free-row collapse nor returns exact algebraic endpoints tied to explicit relational SCM witnesses. The missing proof must show that repeated target occurrences use the same q, source compatibility fixes all other rows, and every q in [0,1] is attainable by a common finite-noise RSCM; otherwise optimizing the formal polynomial does not establish sharpness for the relational model class.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if sharpness theorem identifying the causal set as F([0,1]), an exact endpoint algorithm comparing F(0), F(1), and F at isolated roots of F', and finite-noise endpoint RSCMs reproducing every source table.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the unseen-combination motivation, relational-SCM language, support boundary, and N3 traffic failure that the sharp-set result should answer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: World models must generalize across varying object configurations -> relational SCMs share mechanisms across skeletons -> missing relational-parent support defeats point identification for N3 -> report the exact set of still-compatible traffic-query values.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the canonical finite-SCM reduction and its proof that optimizing response-function probabilities is equivalent to optimizing over all compatible SCMs, specialized by eliminating every identified row except q.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its equivalence between causal compatibility and a polynomial feasible set is the closest general sharpness argument; the proposed resolution replaces a high-dimensional program by the exact image of one shared row.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the construction that relaxes empirical-distribution equalities to jointly covering constraints and then optimizes the causal polynomial over that confidence region.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the nearest estimator-and-coverage rung for a sharp discrete causal bound, against which an exact one-row population result and its finite-sample outer version can be stated.

open_problems.open_problem: Does there exist a fixed serialized certificate grammar for one-unseen-row relational-SCM bounds whose rational-arithmetic checker is sound and complete for endpoint claims with repeated derivative roots, omitted critical points, boundary ties, algebraic conjugates, and equality of serialized endpoint models to all source laws, with certificate size and checking cost polynomial in the expanded input and grounding?

source_refs.claim: RelationalNeuralID is sound and complete as an abstract identification procedure, but its implemented finite-sample extrema are neural optimization outputs rather than independently checkable exact certificates.
source_refs.author: Adiba Ejaz and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: An untrusted external solver can supply algebraic roots while Isabelle/HOL checks root pinning and polynomial signs through univariate CAD and Sturm-Tarski queries.
source_refs.author: Wenda Li, Grant Olney Passmore, and Lawrence C. Paulson

source_refs.claim: A formally verified PVS procedure decides univariate polynomial systems by Sturm root counting and interval subdivision, with soundness and completeness internal to the prover.
source_refs.author: Anthony Narkawicz, César Muñoz, and Aaron Dutle

source_refs.claim: Exact real-root isolation for integer univariate polynomials, including multiplicities and non-square-free inputs, admits explicit bit-complexity bounds.
source_refs.author: Elias P. Tsigaridas and Ioannis Z. Emiris

open_problems.why_unsolved: Verified-algebra methods supply checkable root isolation and sign determination, but certify statements about supplied polynomials rather than proving that a polynomial was correctly derived from a relational grounding or that a selected algebraic value is realized by a source-compatible RSCM. Relational causal work supplies the model semantics but no proof object linking grounding evaluation, the derivative-root list, endpoint-value ordering, tie handling, and finite-noise witnesses. The new semantic step is to define one grammar whose local checks compose into the global causal sharpness claim and prove that close or repeated roots, boundary coincidences, and conjugate algebraic values do not force super-polynomial certificate expansion.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A concrete certificate syntax and checker together with soundness, completeness, polynomial-size, and polynomial-checking theorems for the chain from source-table compatibility and F(q) derivation through exhaustive critical-point comparison to accepted endpoint RSCMs.

writing_exemplar.why: Its algorithmic identification narrative supplies the causal consumer and explains why a certificate should accompany an N3 fitted result rather than appear as a standalone computer-algebra exercise.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Relational causal models answer queries on unseen skeletons -> optimization tests agreement of compatible models -> unsupported N3 produces nonunique extrema -> replace opaque extrema by a replayable certificate tying each algebraic endpoint to a compatible relational SCM.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse the skeptical architecture in which an untrusted producer supplies algebraic roots and a small trusted checker verifies root selection and signs using Sturm-Tarski computations over rational data.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired endpoint certificate has the same producer-checker split but must add causal-derivation and endpoint-model clauses.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over Sturm root counts, interval subdivision, and the proof that the resulting Boolean decision procedure is sound and complete for combinations of univariate equalities and inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Derivative-root exhaustiveness, positivity, interval membership, and endpoint comparisons reduce to the univariate relation systems handled by this machinery.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exact isolating intervals, multiplicity handling, and coefficient-bit complexity analysis for non-square-free derivative polynomials.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Repeated critical points and polynomial-size accounting are precisely where a naive endpoint-certificate argument needs a mature exact root-isolation bound.

open_problems.open_problem: For sampled supported mechanism rows and one wholly unsupported shared row in a finite Markovian relational SCM, can simultaneous rational confidence boxes be propagated to a conservative confidence outer set for the target causal range with a labeled occurrence-coupling inflation min(1, sum_r m_r epsilon_r), without claiming exact multivariate projection?

source_refs.claim: The practical RSCM implementation replaces population equalities by maximum-likelihood fitting, and Experiment 6.1 reports finite-sample errors that depend on whether exact relational neighborhoods occur in the source.
source_refs.author: Adiba Ejaz and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Bernoulli-KL hyperrectangles give conservative finite-sample coverage for observed probabilities and can be pushed through causal optimization, while nominal-coverage uncertainty quantification is identified as future work.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Minimum-average-volume confidence regions are developed for an iid categorical distribution and linear functionals of its multinomial parameter.
source_refs.author: Matthew L. Malloy, Ardhendu Tripathy, and Robert D. Nowak

source_refs.claim: Confidence regions for set-identified parameters are obtained by inverting sample criteria, with consistency, rates, and coverage results.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing discrete-causal confidence regions cover ordinary observed probability vectors, while the RSCM application estimates type-shared rows that may occur several times in one target grounding. Reusing the same uncertain mechanism row creates semantic dependence not captured by treating target occurrences as fresh iid cells. The missing proof begins by coupling each supported true row to a row inside its rational confidence box, then telescopes discrepancies over the m_r labeled occurrences before ranging over unsupported q. This yields an honest outer set but generally not the exact projection of the full joint confidence region. No surveyed relational-SCM paper provides this separation of sampling uncertainty, repeated-occurrence inflation, and structural non-identification.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample coverage theorem for a computable rational outer interval combining simultaneous row-wise confidence boxes with the perturbation bound min(1, sum_r m_r epsilon_r), while retaining the exact population F([0,1]) component and explicitly labeling the result conservative.

writing_exemplar.why: Its traffic experiment naturally motivates why an RNCM point fit for N3 needs both structural-range and finite-sample uncertainty reporting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Traffic queries must transfer across varying scenes -> shared relational mechanisms allow borrowing source data -> unsupported neighborhoods create structural ambiguity while supported rows remain noisy -> accompany the N3 point fit with a jointly valid, explicitly conservative causal range.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the proof that a jointly covering confidence region for empirical probabilities remains covering after optimizing the causal target over models satisfying the relaxed constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is the relational shared-row analogue of its finite-sample confidence-bound construction, with occurrence-coupling inflation replacing exact projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Use nonasymptotic multinomial confidence-region inversion as the source of simultaneous supported-row uncertainty sets before rational outward rounding.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Supported finite conditional tables are multinomial parameters; their regions provide the primitive coverage event that the relational perturbation theorem must preserve.

method_exemplars.technique: Borrow the distinction between confidence regions for the identified set and confidence regions for individual parameters, proving coverage by inversion of a jointly valid sample criterion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the correct coverage language for reporting a random outer set around a population sharp causal interval.

open_problems.open_problem: For each fixed k greater than one, can k unsupported shared binary context rows in a finite acyclic relational SCM be handled by an exact output-sensitive semialgebraic algorithm that certifies the sharp query image over [0,1]^k, constructs endpoint RSCMs, and gives explicit certificate-size and checking bounds in terms of the expanded relational polynomial program?

source_refs.claim: Relational SCMs share mechanisms across objects and skeletons, but unsupported target configurations are classified as non-identifiable rather than assigned a sharp multivariate compatibility region.
source_refs.author: Adiba Ejaz and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: General discrete counterfactual sharp bounds have a polynomial-program formulation, but solving the resulting programs is computationally expensive and practical bounds use approximation.
source_refs.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, and Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Spatial branch-and-bound yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp answers for multivariate discrete causal programs, with computation time for complex problems identified as a key open direction.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Exact rational weighted-sum-of-squares certificates can be recovered from numerical dual information for positive polynomials on compact semialgebraic sets.
source_refs.author: Maria M. Davis and Dávid Papp

open_problems.why_unsolved: The one-row method's first proof step, enumerating roots of F' on an interval, fails for k rows: extrema may lie on any cube face or on positive-dimensional critical loci, and endpoint-value comparison may require multivariate elimination. General causal polynomial programs and exact positivity certificates cover adjacent pieces, but the targeted scan found no result exploiting a fixed number of unsupported type-shared rows while also producing relational-SCM witnesses and a checkable exact sharp-image certificate. Any positive theorem must state complexity against the expanded grounding and polynomial representation because succinct relational input can hide degree and monomial blow-up.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fixed-k theorem and algorithm enumerating boundary-face and interior critical candidates by exact elimination, comparing their algebraic target values, certifying the resulting interval or finite union, and serializing compatible finite-noise RSCMs attaining every reported endpoint with explicit output-sensitive complexity.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames varying relational neighborhoods as the destination problem; the extension should be presented as graded recovery beyond its binary identifiable-or-nonidentifiable boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Mechanisms are shared across arbitrary relational skeletons -> source support may miss several target contexts -> binary identification failure discards quantitative information -> compute and certify the exact multicontext compatibility range.

method_exemplars.technique: Use canonical finite SCMs to prove that the multivariate polynomial feasible region is causally complete, then quotient response-function coordinates according to shared relational context rows.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the general causal-to-polynomial equivalence that a fixed-k relational specialization must preserve.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt exact rational nonnegativity certificates on compact semialgebraic sets to certify that no point of [0,1]^k improves on a proposed algebraic endpoint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Global endpoint certification is equivalent to nonnegativity of an endpoint-shifted target polynomial on the cube, although extra algebraic-value and RSCM-witness clauses are required.

method_exemplars.technique: Use spatial branch-and-bound and confidence-region relaxation as a numerical producer and finite-sample outer-bound layer while an exact checker validates the fixed-k population certificate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest implemented estimator-and-limit workflow for the same multivariate discrete causal polynomial programs.

literature_map:
Ejaz and Bareinboim (2026, ICML, arXiv:2606.14892) define RSCMs, prove cross-skeleton support criteria, and expose the unsupported N3 traffic failure, but give no sharp set.
Arbour, Garant, and Jensen (2016, KDD, DOI:10.1145/2939672.2939791) extend back-door adjustment to relational domains, assuming the target relational setting is observed.
Salimi et al. (2020, SIGMOD, arXiv:2004.03644) give a declarative causal-relational framework but not cross-skeleton mechanism-level partial identification.
Jensen, Burroni, and Rattigan (2020, UAI, PMLR 115) show object conditioning can identify effects in plate models; this is structurally narrower than varying relational skeletons.
Weinstein and Blei (2024/2026, JMLR, arXiv:2401.05330) develop hierarchical causal models and extended do-calculus, reinforcing that plates can aid identification but not solving unsupported shared rows.
Ahsan, Arbour, and Zheleva (2022, PMLR, arXiv:2202.10706) handle cyclic relational separation and representation, a different boundary from finite acyclic sharp bounds.
Xia et al. (2021, NeurIPS, arXiv:2107.00793) establish neural-SCM expressivity and identification testing, the neural foundation inherited by the RSCM algorithm.
Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022, ICML, arXiv:2110.05690) canonicalize finite SCMs and reduce sharp counterfactual bounds to polynomial programs, but approximate expensive optima.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) provide numerical or epsilon-sharp polynomial bounds, finite-sample confidence relaxations, and flag uncertainty quantification and computation time as open.
Finkelstein and Shpitser (2020, UAI, PMLR 124) derive graphical counterfactual inequalities and sharp bounds by logical event relations, without relational mechanism sharing.
Balke and Pearl (1997, JASA, DOI:10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074) are the foundational exact finite-response-function and linear-program sharp-bound anchor.
Balazadeh, Syrgkanis, and Krishnan (2022, NeurIPS) show neural partial-identification optimization can be unstable and leave finite-sample uncertainty unquantified outside special regimes.
Li, Passmore, and Paulson (2019, JAR, arXiv:1506.08238) and Narkawicz, Muñoz, and Dutle (2018, JFR) establish skeptical, sound and complete checking for univariate polynomial certificates.
Tsigaridas and Emiris (2006, ESA, arXiv:cs/0604066) supply exact root-isolation and multiplicity complexity; Davis and Papp (2022, SIOPT) supply exact rational polynomial-positivity certificates.
Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, arXiv:2002.01044) and Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007, Econometrica) supply the multinomial and set-inference pieces, but not repeated relational-occurrence coupling.
